answer: Verified Work Ledger: each identity must complete real tasks whose outputs are spot-checked against hidden reference answers, and only verified work earns the pearl credits agents spend to act. A new identity starts with zero credits, so it must first do unpaid verifiable labor, each task carrying an opal verification token tied to its submission. Duplicate or copied answers fail checks and forfeit the violet completion mark, blocking credit. An attacker running N sybils must perform N distinct verified tasks before any acts, a per-identity labor cost that scales linearly and cannot be bought.
